name: Jehoash
bio:
Jehoash (Joash), son of Jehoahaz, became king of Israel in Samaria and reigned sixteen years, doing evil in the LORD's eyes like Jeroboam before him (2 Kings 13:10-11). When Elisha lay dying, Jehoash came to him weeping, calling him "my father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof." Elisha had him shoot an arrow eastward as a sign of victory over Syria, then told him to strike the ground with his remaining arrows; Jehoash struck only three times, and Elisha, angry, told him he should have struck five or six times for complete victory — now he would only defeat Syria three times (2 Kings 13:14-19). After Hazael died and his son Ben-Hadad succeeded him, Jehoash recovered the Israelite cities Hazael had taken from his father Jehoahaz, defeating Ben-Hadad three times exactly as Elisha had foretold (2 Kings 13:22-25).

## 📖 Core Story: War Against Amaziah

When Amaziah, king of Judah, flush with victory over Edom, challenged Jehoash to meet him in battle, Jehoash sent back a parable comparing Amaziah to a thistle foolishly provoking a cedar, and warned him to stay home and enjoy his glory rather than bring disaster on himself and Judah. Amaziah refused to listen, and the two met at Beth Shemesh, where Judah was routed. Jehoash captured Amaziah, marched to Jerusalem, tore down four hundred cubits of its wall from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, and carried off all the gold, silver, and temple vessels he could find, along with hostages, before returning to Samaria (2 Kings 14:8-14). Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria; his son Jeroboam succeeded him (2 Kings 14:15-16).
